catalog: fit-food-core.sqlite, the file production opens by default (data/db/fit-food-core.sqlite); no Open Food Facts or CNF rows

pageFill.note: the largest page /api/foods will serve (MAX_LIMIT in src/lib/server/catalog/foods.ts), because the duplicate-name collapse empties the tail of a page rather than its first rows. These queries carry no acceptable or forbidden names: what each is owed is read out of the catalog on the run, so a rebuilt catalog moves the expectation with it instead of failing the fixture.

queries.means: the deepest collapse in the catalog: several hundred branded rows are all named ICE CREAM, and the generic ice cream family sits below them
a jarred staple whose branded rows share a handful of names, and the second-deepest collapse measured
the query #106 was reported on: it answered with one food when the collapse ran after the page was cut
724 rows carry its top name, the deepest need DEDUP_DEPTH was originally measured against
the collapse's own example: five dairies' rows all named MILK must read as one food and leave room for the rest

note: acceptable and forbidden names are what a person typing the query means, not what the ranking answers today. Every name is checked to exist in the catalog before a run is scored, so a typo fails the run rather than silently lowering the score.
